images.note: 8''-wide square continuum cutout (286-294 GHz, mfs image of the 286-298 GHz high-sideband data of the 302 GHz IF; SMA 302 GHz LO synthesized beam ~1.0'' FWHM, Sec. 3.3). Shows the 2.06''-separated G6 binary DoAr 24E as two distinct compact peaks: the brighter DoAr 24Ea (upper right, peak ~36 mJy beam^-1 read off the 0-43 mJy beam^-1 colour scale) and fainter DoAr 24Eb (lower left); both are unresolved point-like blobs at this resolution (Table 1 gives R_95% = 0.098'' for Ea and 0.024'' for Eb, i.e. below the SMA beam, and Sec. 3.4.1 states both were fitted as point sources). Visibility-fit flux densities at 294 GHz: Ea 36.6 +/- 4.9 mJy, Eb 24.8 +/- 4.9 mJy (Table 5). At <=230 GHz the two components are confused on their 2.06'' separation. The 286-298 GHz data come from the SMA 270 GHz tracks 270GHz-2a (2022-05-23, EXT) and 270GHz-1 (2023-08-29, COM); the paper does not state which track covered which target.

notes: Binary in Ophiuchus: the optically visible primary DoAr 24 E and its infrared companion (DoAr 24E IRC) show roughly equal 880 um emission, both imaged in the pre-ALMA SMA survey (Andrews et al. 2010).
